narrative:
The model predicts you have a 13% chance of failing your final year, which is low enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution to help you succeed.

The prediction that you might fail is driven mainly by three aspects of your background. The most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. Surprisingly, this actually pushed the model toward expecting you to fail. Among students who passed, having zero previous failures is the average, yet in your specific combination of circumstances the model interpreted the absence of any prior setbacks as a signal that you may be at higher risk now.

The second most important influence was your strong desire to pursue higher education. This worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward passing, which makes sense because every student who ultimately passed also expressed this same ambition.

The third key factor was your father's education level, which is only primary school. This pushed the prediction toward failing. Compared with students who passed, where only 13.8% had fathers educated only to primary level, your situation stands out as less common and contributed to the model's caution.

To improve, focus on building consistent study habits now, seek extra academic support early, and talk with your teachers about targeted help in any subjects where you feel less confident. Taking the remedial courses seriously can turn this small risk into a clear success. (248 words)
